# How to Get Quick Summaries from Long Documents with Claude

Ever feel swamped by lengthy reports, articles, or complex documents? This guide will show you how to use Claude, an **AI (Artificial Intelligence)**, which is like a very smart computer program designed to think and learn, to quickly get the main points from almost any text. By the end, you'll be able to upload a document and ask Claude to summarise it for you, giving you the essential information you need in a flash.

## Before you start
- You'll need a free Claude account (or a paid plan if you prefer). This will give you access to Claude's website.
- Access to the Claude website through your computer's web browser.
- A digital document you want to summarise, such as a PDF or a plain text file. Note that Claude has limits on the file size and length it can process, but free plans are usually sufficient for most common documents.
- This whole process should take you about 5-7 minutes.

## Step 1 — Access Claude's Website
Your first step is to open your web browser and navigate to the Claude website. Think of Claude as a powerful **Large Language Model (LLM)**, which is like the highly intelligent engine behind an AI, specifically designed to understand and generate human language. You'll usually see a clean, welcoming chat interface where you can begin interacting with the AI.

You'll know it worked when you see a main chat area, often with a text box at the bottom ready for you to type in.

## Step 2 — Start a New Conversation
To ensure you're starting fresh, it's a good idea to begin a new conversation with Claude. Look for a "New Chat" button, which is commonly found on the left-hand side of the screen or near the top. Clicking this will give you a clean slate, meaning Claude won't carry over any previous topics or instructions from old chats, so your summary request will be clear.

If it looks different on your screen, don't worry! Apps change often. You might see a small plus (+) icon, or a menu option like "Start new conversation." Simply click whatever seems to open a fresh chat.

You'll know it worked when the main chat window is clear, with no previous messages, and the message box at the bottom is empty, waiting for your input.

## Step 3 — Upload Your Document
Now it's time to get your document into Claude. Look for a paperclip icon, usually found near the message box where you type. This icon is universally used for attachments. Clicking it will open your computer's file explorer, allowing you to browse and select the PDF or text file you wish to summarise. Claude can handle various formats, but PDFs and plain text are generally the most reliable for summarisation. Remember, very large files might not upload on a free plan, as Claude, like all AIs, has a **context window** – this is like the AI's short-term memory, limiting how much text it can 'remember' at once.

If you don't see a paperclip, look for an "Attach file" text link or a similar icon that suggests adding a file.

You'll know it worked when the name of your uploaded document appears in the message box, usually next to your cursor, indicating it's ready to be sent.

## Step 4 — Craft Your Summary Request
With your document attached, it's time to tell Claude what you want. This instruction is called a **prompt**, which is simply the command you give to the AI. In the message box, type out a clear request for a summary. Being specific helps Claude understand exactly what you're looking for, rather than just giving a generic overview. For instance, you could ask for specific details or a summary tailored to a particular audience.

If your message box is hard to find, it’s usually a long, horizontal bar at the very bottom of the chat window.

You'll know it worked when your complete summary request appears in the message box, ready to be sent to Claude.
💬 Example: "Please summarise this document for me, highlighting the main points and key takeaways relevant to small businesses."

## Step 5 — Send Your Request
Once your document is attached and your summary request is typed, the next step is to send it to Claude. Look for a "Send" button or a paper plane icon, usually located at the right end of the message box. Clicking this will submit both your document and your prompt to the AI. Claude will then begin processing the information, reading through your document and generating a summary based on your instructions. This process usually happens quite quickly.

If the button looks different, it might be an arrow or just the word "Send". Just click the button that looks like it will submit your message.

You'll know it worked when your message disappears from the box, and Claude's response starts appearing in the main chat window, beginning with your requested summary.

## Step 6 — Review and Refine the Summary
After Claude generates the summary, take a moment to read through it. AI responses are usually very helpful, but sometimes they might not hit every single point you need, or you might want more detail on a specific section. This is where you can interact further. If you need more information or a different perspective, just type another prompt in the message box, referring back to the document or the summary Claude just gave you. For example, you could ask Claude to elaborate on a particular section or rephrase the summary for a different audience.

If the answer isn't quite what you expected, don't worry, that's normal with AIs. Just try rephrasing your question or adding more specific details in your next prompt.

You'll know it worked when you've either received a summary that fully meets your needs or have asked follow-up questions that yield the specific additional information you were looking for.
💬 Example: "Can you list the top three challenges mentioned in the document and suggest potential solutions?"

## Step 7 — Save or Copy Your Summary
Once you're happy with Claude's summary, you'll likely want to save or copy it for your own use. You can typically highlight the text of Claude's response using your mouse, then right-click and select "Copy." You can then paste this summary into a document, email, or wherever you need it. Some AI tools also offer specific "Copy" buttons next to their responses or even export options, though these vary.

If you don't see a direct "copy" button, highlighting the text and using your computer's standard copy (Ctrl+C on Windows, Command+C on Mac) and paste (Ctrl+V or Command+V) functions will always work.

You'll know it worked when you've successfully pasted the summary into another application or saved it to a file, making it ready for your tasks.

## Common mistakes
-   **Uploading unsupported files or files that are too large:** Claude works best with common document types like PDFs, Word documents, and text files. If you try to upload an image or a video, or a document that's many hundreds of pages long, it might not work.
    *   **The fix:** Convert your file to a supported format like PDF or plain text. If it's very long, you might need to split it into smaller sections or use a paid plan with a larger context window.
-   **Vague summary requests:** Just saying "Summarise this" might give you a general overview, but it might not be what you actually need. Claude is good, but it can't read your mind!
    *   **The fix:** Be specific! Ask for "three key takeaways," "a summary for someone who knows nothing about this topic," or "the pros and cons of this proposal." The more detail you give in your **prompt**, the better the result.
-   **Not verifying critical information:** While Claude is powerful, it's an AI and can sometimes **hallucinate**, which is when an AI confidently presents false or inaccurate information as if it were true. It generates text based on patterns, not absolute truth.
    *   **The fix:** Always cross-check any critical facts, figures, or sensitive information from the summary with the original document or another reliable source, especially if you plan to use the summary for important decisions. Claude can draft an excellent summary, but it can't verify the truthfulness of *every single detail* for you, especially in complex or niche topics.

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** Imagine quickly understanding the long terms and conditions for a new app, getting the gist of a lengthy news article, or grasping the main points of a new recipe or instruction manual without reading every single word. Claude can save you precious time.
-   **For your business or work:** This skill is invaluable for professionals. You can rapidly review lengthy reports, condense meeting minutes, extract key findings from research papers, or quickly understand client briefs, allowing you to focus on decision-making rather than sifting through pages of text.
-   **If you're just getting started:** Pick a news article you're interested in online. Copy the main text, paste it into a new Claude conversation, and ask, "Summarise this for me in three sentences." It's a quick, easy way to get a feel for how it works!

## Try it now
Find a short PDF document (perhaps a product manual or a short article) or copy-paste the text from a recent online news story into Claude, and then ask it to "Give me the top three main points from this text." See how quickly you can get to the core information!
